title: Microwave stewardship timetable and experiment notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact 3-day microwave launch stewardship plan, experimental toggles for throughput tuning, a lightweight rollout timetable (hourly during the first day, then stepped), and a short-form release-notes draft to hand to docs/CS. It's intentionally a field notebook: checklists, unresolved questions, sampling numbers and quick rollback decision heuristics.

Context and goals:
- Target: push lightweight serving runtime update (kernel selector + local KV-cache tweak) to hosted and dedicated pools.
- Objective: validate that the new kernel selection reduces tail latency for long-seq requests (>512 tokens) without regressing 95th latency for short-seq (<64 tokens).
- Success criteria (primary): 95th latency for short-seq does not increase >5% and long-seq latency reduces by >=10% on representative load.
- Secondary: token compute efficiency improves by at least 6% (measured server-side token counters).

High-level timeline (UTC):
Day -2 (prep)
- Confirm smoke tests and post-deploy probes (see Smoke & Telemetry checklist).
- Lock release notes draft and update internal config flags.
- Cut build and tag: redwood-inference/runtime:v2026.10-microwave-1
- Run local canary simulation against staging for 2h (synthetic mix: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long).

Day -1 (dry run)
- 09:00: Dry-run cutover in staging; ops, SRE and release steward on call. Validate perf signals and observability dashboards.
- 14:00: Run degradation scenarios (KV miss storm; slow disk) and record behavior in incident notebook.

Day 0 (launch)
- 08:00: Preflight sync call (15m): go/no-go checklist.
- 08:15: Holdback lane enabled (0% traffic).
- 08:30: Stage rollout to 1% sampled traffic across one region (EU-west1) and dedicated pool A.
- 09:30: If no regressions, expand to 5% EU-west1 + 1% us-west1.
- 11:30: Telemetry check-in: perf owners (+ SRE) evaluate KPIs and decide on 25% expansion.
- 14:00: If green, expand to 25% worldwide split: 60% hosted, 40% dedicated.
- 18:00: Progress to 50% if metrics remain stable.
- 22:00: Nightly assessment; keep steward on call until 02:00 UTC.

Day 1 (stabilize)
- 08:00: Full telemetry review; expand to 75% if no alerts and token efficiency stable.
- 16:00: Optional: full rollout to 100% if final checks pass.
- 20:00: Post-rollout debrief; populate the release-notes and deployment log.

Day 2-3 (post-mortem & cleanup)
- Collect extended regressions, update model routing fallback entries, and archive experiment toggles.

Smoke & Telemetry checklist (preflight & continuous probes):
- Smoke tests (automated): basic generation, chat flow, embeddings retrieval, batch routing.
- Load probes: 30s spikes at 2x baseline every 2h during day 0.
- Correctness checks: golden prompt set of 120 prompts across short/med/long sequences. Compare top-1 output hashes and token-level divergence metrics (>10% divergence triggers manual review).
- Latency buckets: P50, P95, P99 for short (<64), med (64-512), long (>512).
- Error rates: 5xxs, 4xx unexpected, rate-limited responses. Thresholds: 5xx >0.02% -> immediate holdback.
- Cost telemetry: tokens/core-second, GPU utilization by job, inference queue depth.

Experiment toggles and parameters to test (annotated):
- KernelSelectorMode: heuristic_v2 (default) | heuristic_v2-conservative | neural-probe
- KVCacheRetention: 8s | 16s | 32s (aim: test TTL vs latency tradeoff)
- BatchWindowMs: 2 | 4 | 8 (observe latency vs throughput delta)
- AggressiveQuantProfile: on | off (for dedicated pools only)

Suggested sampling matrix (quick):
- Phase A (1%): 100% heuristic_v2 (baseline tunnel), KVCacheRetention=8s, BatchWindowMs=4
- Phase B (5-25%): run parallel split 80/20: baseline vs KernelSelectorMode=neural-probe (A/B test).
- Phase C (25%+): if neural-probe is superior AND no regressions, flip default to neural-probe with conservative backing for short-seq traffic.

Rollback decision ladder (short):
- Immediate rollback (auto): 5xx rate >0.02% sustained for 3 mins OR P95(short) increases >15% vs baseline for 10 mins.
- Manual rollback candidate: degradation in top-1 correctness hashes for golden prompts >6% over 30m window. Requires steward + SRE approval.
- Throttle back option: reduce rollout percentage by half and enable conservative kernel for short-seq (mitigates transient spikes).

Responsibilities (quick roster):
- Release steward: Aisha Patel (primary) — coordinated call, final go/no-go, release-note handoff.
- SRE lead: Diego Morales — telemetry, alert triage, runbook execution.
- Performance engineer: Priya Srinivasan — interpret latency histograms and token efficiency.
- Dev owner: Jonah Kim — patch rollouts, quick hotfix PRs.
- CS liaison: Maren Lowe (notify enterprise customers if any dedicated customers are affected).

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Preflight Slack: "[RELEASE] Microwave launch v2026.10 scheduled at 08:00 UTC today. Steward: @Aisha. SRE on-call: @Diego. Quick-checks: smoke, golden prompts, latency buckets. Reply ACK to join 08:00 sync."
- Rollback alert: "[AUTO-ROLLBACK] v2026.10 triggered auto-rollback at {time} UTC: 5xx > threshold. Engineers: stand by for incident triage."
- Internal release-note snippet (draft to docs/CS):
  - Title: Runtime kernel-selection improvement (v2026.10)
  - Short blurb: Tuned kernel-selection heuristics and KV-cache defaults to reduce tail latency on long sequences; focused rollout and A/B experiments carried out on 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07.
  - Known issues: conservative impact on a tiny subset of short-seq traffic during aggressive quant profile testing (mitigated).

Release notes (hand-off draft):
- Summary: We deployed kernel selection and KV-cache tuning aimed at improving long-seq P95 latencies. The change was rolled out incrementally with A/B testing. Overall long-seq P95 improved by ~12% on average while maintaining short-seq P95 within the 5% target.
- Rollout: 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07, incremental 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% (finalized at 2026-10-06 16:40 UTC).
- Telemetry highlights: long-seq P95 down 12%; token compute efficiency +6.4%; no sustained increase in 5xxs.
- Rollback events: One automated holdback at 2026-10-05 09:12 UTC triggered by intermittent disk timeout in eu-west1; rollout resumed after disk remediation and conservative kernel applied to eu-west1.
- Action items: follow-up perf tuning for BatchWindowMs under high-cold-cache conditions.

Post-release checklist:
- Archive experiment toggles and label the A/B results in the experiment registry.
- Run 72h extended correctness check across golden prompts and surface any drift to product/ML.
- Create a small runbook entry for kernelSelectorMode=neural-probe to be used in future rollouts.
- Update canary simulation harness with the new long-seq scenarios we observed in wild traffic.

Unresolved questions / notes-to-self:
- neural-probe: how does model-architecture variance affect the selector thresholds? Need sample from 3 different model families. (Priya to schedule)
- Should we gate AggressiveQuantProfile to dedicated pools only permanently? initial results show cost wins but a mild uptick in subtle token divergences.
- Follow-up: validate interactions between BatchWindowMs=2 and autoscaler cooldowns (observed slight over-scaling risk).

Quick links (for ops in-call):
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/staging-runtime
- Prod dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/prod-runtime
- Experiment registry: https://confluence.redwood.ai/experiments/MW-21
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- Incident runbook (latency): https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/latency-p95

Appendix: short-form hourly watchlist for Day 0 (UTC)
08:30 - initial 1% check: P50/P95/P99, 5xx rate, golden prompt pass rate
09:30 - 1h traffic window: investigate any 5xx spikes, compare med/long-seq buckets
11:30 - 3h window: A/B experiment results snapshot; decision to expand to 25%
14:00 - mid-day health: token efficiency and GPU utilization check
18:00 - evening ramp: decide on 50% progression or hold
22:00 - night snapshot: prepare night steward and handoff notes

Change log (quick):
- 2026-10-05: created draft and initial timetable.
- 2026-10-06: updated with Day 0 outcomes and minor rollback incident note.
- 2026-10-12: refined rollback thresholds and added appendix hourly watchlist.

End of notebook.

TODOs (triage list):
- [ ] Priya: run architecture-sensitivity matrix for neural-probe by 2026-10-14
- [ ] Diego: validate alert run params and lower 5xx alert threshold in prod for this rollout window by 2026-10-09
- [ ] Jonah: prepare quick-patch branch to demote AggressiveQuantProfile if regressions appear (PR template under PR#4521).
- [ ] Aisha: sync with CS on dedicated-customer notice template (target 2026-10-07).
